newsitem.title: CHINA: HK BLUE CHIPS END WEAK, FOCUS ON CHINA STOCKS.
newsitem.headline: HK BLUE CHIPS END WEAK, FOCUS ON CHINA STOCKS.

text.p: Hong Kong blue chips ended only modestly higher on Thursday while locally-listed red chips and China's B shares rallied as investors continued to seek exposure to the Chinese market.

"The action is still in China-related stocks. Obviously the first tier stocks are not on the move so the Hang Seng Index was relatively sluggish," said Eugene Law, associate director at Lippo Securities.
The Hang Seng Index rose 14.78 points, or 0.09 percent, to 16,497.71. The red chip Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index jumped 52.83 points, or 1.37 percent, to 3,913.45.

A flood of liquidity rushed into China on Thursday driving Shanghai's foreign currency B shares up 7.227 points, or 9.86 percent, to close at 80.496, while Shenzhen's B share index jumped 13.78 points to its 10 percent limit-up level of 151.22.
But a recent surge in Hong Kong-listed Chinese enterprises waned with the H-share index closing down 18.46 points, or 1.21 percent, at 1,510.24.

"It is rotational, cyclical buying," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities. "Investors have come to the end of the road where they have traded everything in Hong Kong that there is to trade, so they go to B shares," he said.
Red chip Kah Bank topped the actives list on Thursday and gained HK$2.25, or 20.64 percent, to HK$13.15.

The company said it was considering becoming wholly-owned subsidiary of a new holding company, spurring hopes that Ka Wah parent China International Trust and Investment Corp may expand the company by injecting new assets into the holding company.
Other small banking shares soared with Liu Chong Hing Bank gaining HK$2.30 to HK$23.00 and Wing Hang Bank up HK$1.00 at HK$47.60.
HSBC Holdings was also strong, rising HK$3.00 to HK$277.00 but other blue chips came under pressure.
Swire Pacific fell HK$1.25 to HK$70.00 and New World Development dropped HK$1.00 to HK$55.00.
"The problem with blue chips is that should we see a continuation of Wall Street's stuttering, they will suffer the most," said Remington.

Hopewell gained HK$0.60 to HK$5.30 amid speculation that China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd could take a stake in the company and that Hopewell may spin off certain operations. Hopewell was not immediately available for comment.
Overall turnover was HK$29.11 billion compared with HK$28.17 billion on Wednesday. -- Jennifer Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
